Event Study and Parallel Trends Validation¶

Thesis: When Governments Say Green - Do Bond Markets Believe Them? Author: Nahian Ibnat | Supervisor: Zoltan Csaba Toth Institution: Central European University | Date: April 2026

Purpose¶

This notebook has two jobs:

Job 1 - Parallel Trends Test (H3 identification) The DiD estimator in M5 requires that treated and control units would have followed the same trend absent treatment. The event study tests this by estimating a separate coefficient per week around the treatment date. Flat, insignificant pre-event coefficients validate the assumption.

Job 2 - H2 Directional Validation The regression shows noise correlates with greenium. This notebook tests direction: does noise lead greenium, or vice versa? This matters because H2 claims political ambiguity causes bond pricing, not the reverse.

1.4 - Helper functions and chart styling¶

In [4]:
def load_bond_ytm(filepath):
    """Load Refinitiv bond file. Mid-YTM = (BidYld + AskYld) / 2."""
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(filepath)
    ws = wb.active
    rows = list(ws.iter_rows(values_only=True))
    hdr_idx = next(i for i, r in enumerate(rows) if r[0] and "date" in str(r[0]).lower())
    df = pd.DataFrame([r for r in rows[hdr_idx+1:] if r[0] is not None], columns=rows[hdr_idx])
    df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Date"])
    df["ytm"]  = (df["BidYld"] + df["AskYld"]) / 2
    return df[["date","ytm"]].dropna().sort_values("date").reset_index(drop=True)

def load_fx(filepath, col_name):
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(filepath)
    ws = wb.active
    rows = list(ws.iter_rows(values_only=True))
    hdr_idx = next(i for i, r in enumerate(rows)
                   if r[0] and "exchange date" in str(r[0]).lower())
    df = pd.DataFrame([r for r in rows[hdr_idx+1:] if r[0] is not None], columns=rows[hdr_idx])
    df["date"]   = pd.to_datetime(df["Exchange Date"])
    df[col_name] = (df["Bid"] + df["Ask"]) / 2
    return df[["date", col_name]].dropna().sort_values("date")

def load_cds(filepath, col_name):
    df = pd.read_csv(filepath)
    df.columns = ["date", col_name, "open", "high", "low", "chg"]
    df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["date"])
    return df[["date", col_name]].dropna()

def style_ax(ax):
    ax.set_facecolor('white')
    ax.tick_params(colors=GRAY, labelsize=8)
    ax.xaxis.label.set_color(GRAY); ax.yaxis.label.set_color(GRAY)
    ax.title.set_color(WHITE)
    for spine in ax.spines.values(): spine.set_edgecolor("#cccccc")
    ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False); ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)

Part 2 - Data Loading and Panel Construction¶

This pipeline mirrors the regression notebook exactly. The one critical fix here is that India's treatment dummy now uses 2023-10-27 (second auction), not 2023-01-25 (inaugural auction). The CDS forward-fill is also applied to handle India's 117 missing CDS days, preventing NaN propagation into the event study regressions.

2.1 - Bond yields and greenium¶

In [5]:
bond_dfs = {}
for key, fpath in BOND_FILES.items():
    bond_dfs[key] = load_bond_ytm(fpath)

panels = []
for gkey, ckey, country, tenor in PAIRS:
    g = bond_dfs[gkey].rename(columns={"ytm": "ytm_green"})
    c = bond_dfs[ckey].rename(columns={"ytm": "ytm_conv"})
    m = pd.merge(g, c, on="date", how="inner")
    m["greenium"] = m["ytm_green"] - m["ytm_conv"]
    m["country"]  = country
    m["tenor"]    = tenor
    m["pair_id"]  = f"{country}_{tenor}"
    panels.append(m)

panel = pd.concat(panels, ignore_index=True)
print(f"Raw panel: {len(panel):,} obs")
print(panel.groupby(["country","tenor"]).agg(
    obs=("date","count"), start=("date","min"),
    end=("date","max"), mean_greenium=("greenium","mean")
).round(4).to_string())

indo_p  = panel[panel["country"]=="Indonesia"].merge(sent_indo, on="date", how="left")

2.3 - First-differencing and standardisation¶

In [7]:
panel = panel.sort_values(["pair_id","date"]).reset_index(drop=True)

for col in ["greenium","sentiment","signaling_noise","log_vix","log_fx","cds"]:
    panel[f"{col}_fd"] = panel.groupby("pair_id")[col].diff()

panel_fd = panel.dropna(subset=["greenium_fd"]).reset_index(drop=True)

for col in ["sentiment_fd","signaling_noise_fd","log_vix_fd","log_fx_fd","cds_fd"]:
    mu = panel_fd[col].mean(); sd = panel_fd[col].std()
    panel_fd[f"{col}_z"] = (panel_fd[col] - mu) / sd if sd > 0 else 0.0

print("NaN check on key columns after CDS fix:")
for col in ["greenium_fd","cds_fd_z","log_vix_fd_z","sentiment_fd_z"]:
    print(f"  {col:<25} NaN={panel_fd[col].isna().sum()}")
print(f"\nFirst-differenced panel: {len(panel_fd):,} obs")

Part 3 - Event Study: Pooled Asia (India + Indonesia)¶

Model specification¶

The pooled event study estimates:

547\Delta \text{Greenium}{i,t} = \sum{k \neq -1} \beta_k D^{(k)}{i,t} + \alpha_i + \varepsilon{i,t}547

where ^{(k)}_{i,t} = 1$ when observation $ is $ weeks relative to that country's own treatment date. Week -1 is the omitted reference category.

Pair fixed effects ($\alpha_i$) are included to absorb the India vs Indonesia level difference in greeniums (India mean ~ +0.005 pp, Indonesia mean ~ -0.069 pp). Without pair FE, the constant conflates two structurally different markets.

Important limitation: The two treatment events are 11 months apart (Nov 2022 vs Oct 2023). Pooling gives an average dynamic response. Country-specific results in Parts 4 and 5 are the primary causal estimates.

3.1 - Assign event time¶

In [8]:
panel_es = panel_fd.copy()
panel_es["event_time"] = np.nan

for country, treat_date in TREATMENT_DATES.items():
    mask          = panel_es["country"] == country
    country_dates = np.sort(panel_es.loc[mask, "date"].unique())
    treat_idx     = np.searchsorted(country_dates, np.datetime64(treat_date))
    date_to_event = {d: int(i - treat_idx) for i, d in enumerate(country_dates)}
    panel_es.loc[mask, "event_time"] = panel_es.loc[mask, "date"].map(date_to_event)

panel_es["event_week"] = (panel_es["event_time"] / 5).apply(np.floor).astype(int)

WEEK_MIN, WEEK_MAX = -10, 10
panel_es = panel_es[panel_es["event_week"].between(WEEK_MIN, WEEK_MAX)].copy()

print(f"Pooled event study: {len(panel_es):,} obs in weeks {WEEK_MIN} to {WEEK_MAX}")
print(f"Reference category: week -1 (week immediately before treatment)")
print(f"\nObs by country:")
print(panel_es.groupby("country")["event_week"].describe()[["count","min","max"]].to_string())

3.2 - Pooled event study regression¶

In [9]:
event_dummies = pd.get_dummies(panel_es["event_week"].astype(str),
                               drop_first=False, dtype=float)
if "-1" in event_dummies.columns:
    event_dummies = event_dummies.drop(columns=["-1"])

panel_es_reg = pd.concat([panel_es, event_dummies], axis=1)
event_cols   = list(event_dummies.columns)

# Pair FE - critical for pooled regression across two markets
pair_dummies_es = pd.get_dummies(panel_es_reg["pair_id"], drop_first=True, dtype=float)
panel_es_reg    = pd.concat([panel_es_reg, pair_dummies_es], axis=1)
fe_cols_es      = list(pair_dummies_es.columns)

X_es     = sm.add_constant(panel_es_reg[event_cols + fe_cols_es])
model_es = OLS(panel_es_reg["greenium_fd"], X_es).fit(cov_type="HC3")

print(f"Pooled event study: N={int(model_es.nobs):,}  R2={model_es.rsquared:.4f}")
print(f"Durbin-Watson: {durbin_watson(model_es.resid):.4f}")

all_weeks = sorted(range(WEEK_MIN, WEEK_MAX + 1))
coefs, ci_lo, ci_hi, pvals = [], [], [], []
ci = model_es.conf_int(alpha=0.05)

for w in all_weeks:
    col = str(w)
    if col in model_es.params.index:
        coefs.append(model_es.params[col])
        ci_lo.append(ci.loc[col, 0])
        ci_hi.append(ci.loc[col, 1])
        pvals.append(model_es.pvalues[col])
    else:
        coefs.append(0.0); ci_lo.append(0.0); ci_hi.append(0.0); pvals.append(1.0)

print("\nPOOLED EVENT STUDY COEFFICIENTS")
print("=" * 60)
print(f"{'Week':<8} {'Period':<10} {'Coef':>10} {'CI Lo':>10} {'CI Hi':>10} {'Sig':>6}")
print("-" * 60)
for w, c, lo, hi, p in zip(all_weeks, coefs, ci_lo, ci_hi, pvals):
    period = "Pre " if w < -1 else "Ref " if w == -1 else "Post"
    ref    = "(ref)" if w == -1 else ("***" if p<0.01 else "**" if p<0.05 else "*" if p<0.1 else "")
    print(f"{w:<8} {period:<10} {c:>+10.5f} {lo:>10.5f} {hi:>10.5f} {ref:>6}")
print("\n * p<0.1  ** p<0.05  *** p<0.01  |  HC3 SE  |  Ref: week -1  |  Pair FE included")

Part 4 - Event Study: India Only¶

Treatment: Second Sovereign Green Bond Auction - 27 October 2023¶

Why the second auction and not the inaugural? India's green bond (IN0020220144) first traded 27 January 2023. If we used that date as the treatment event, there would be zero pre-treatment greenium observations

  • the bond did not exist in secondary markets before that date. The second auction

(27 October 2023) provides approximately 120 trading days of genuine pre-treatment greenium data (late January 2023 to late October 2023), making it the only valid H3 treatment event for India.

Economic interpretation: The second auction signals programme permanence - the government is not treating the green bond as a one-off gesture but as a recurring financing instrument. H3 tests whether this credibility signal is priced into the greenium.

Note on pair FE: India has one bond pair. Pair FE are collinear with the constant and are correctly omitted. The constant absorbs the baseline level.

4.1 - Assign event time (India)¶

In [11]:
panel_ind_es = panel_fd[panel_fd["country"]=="India"].copy().reset_index(drop=True)

treat_date_ind = TREATMENT_DATES["India"]
country_dates  = np.sort(panel_ind_es["date"].unique())

Part 5 - Event Study: Indonesia Only¶

Treatment: JETP Announcement at G20 Bali - 15 November 2022¶

Economic context: The Just Energy Transition Partnership committed USD 20 billion in international climate financing to Indonesia - the largest such pledge to a single emerging market at the time. H3 tests whether this internationally-backed credibility signal produced a structural greenium widening.

Pre-treatment data limitation: Indonesia's conventional twin (US455780DN36) started trading in September 2022, leaving only approximately 55 trading days before the November 2022 treatment. The pre-event window is therefore truncated. Early event-week coefficients (weeks -10 to -8) may be missing or imprecise due to this constraint. This limitation is acknowledged as a caveat on the Indonesia parallel trends test.

Part 7 - Formal Parallel Trends Test (Joint F-Test)¶

Why a formal test?¶

Eyeballing the event study chart for pre-event flatness is subjective. A joint F-test on all pre-event dummy coefficients is the formal standard.

Null hypothesis: All pre-event week coefficients equal zero (parallel trends holds).

547H_0: \beta_k = 0 \quad \forall, k \in {-10, -9, ..., -2}547

Failure to reject (p > 0.10) means we cannot statistically distinguish the pre-event trend from zero - supporting the parallel trends assumption.

Reference: Roth, J. (2022). Pre-test with caution: Event-study estimates after testing for parallel trends. American Economic Review: Insights, 4(3), 305-322.

In [18]:
def formal_pretrend_test(model, all_weeks, label):
    """Joint F-test on all pre-event week dummies (weeks < -1)."""
    pre_cols = [str(w) for w in all_weeks if w < -1 and str(w) in model.params.index]
    
    if not pre_cols:
        print(f"[{label}] No pre-event dummies available.")
        return

    wald  = model.wald_test(pre_cols, use_f=True)
    f_stat = float(wald.statistic)
    p_val  = float(wald.pvalue)
    df1    = len(pre_cols)
    
    result = "SUPPORTED (cannot reject H0)" if p_val > 0.1 else "VIOLATED (pre-trend detected)"
    
    print(f"\n[{label}]")
    print(f"  Pre-event dummies tested: {pre_cols}")
    print(f"  Joint F({df1}, {int(model.df_resid)}) = {f_stat:.4f}  p = {p_val:.4f}")
    print(f"  Parallel trends: {result}")
    print(f"  Individual pre-event coefficients:")
    for col in pre_cols:
        c = model.params[col]; p = model.pvalues[col]
        s = "***" if p<0.01 else "**" if p<0.05 else "*" if p<0.1 else "n.s."
        print(f"    Week {col:>4}: beta={c:+.5f}  p={p:.3f}  {s}")

print("FORMAL PARALLEL TRENDS TESTS - JOINT F-TEST")
print("=" * 65)
print("H0: All pre-event week coefficients = 0 (parallel trends holds)")
print("Reject if p < 0.10")

formal_pretrend_test(model_es,  all_weeks,     "POOLED")
formal_pretrend_test(model_ind, all_weeks_ind, "INDIA")
formal_pretrend_test(model_ido, all_weeks_ido, "INDONESIA")

print()
print("GUIDANCE:")
print("  India has ~120 trading days pre-event - reliable test.")
print("  Indonesia has ~55 trading days pre-event - limited power.")
print("  A failed F-test (p < 0.10) means DiD estimates are biased.")

Part 8 - H2 Directional Validation: Lead-Lag and Granger Causality¶

Why H2 needs its own check¶

M3 in the regression notebook shows signaling noise correlates with the greenium. Correlation does not establish direction. H2 claims: political ambiguity causes bond pricing changes. Two tests validate the direction.

Test 1 - Lead-lag event study around high-noise episodes: If noise causes greenium changes, greenium should be flat before noise spikes. High-noise days are defined as signaling_noise above the 75th percentile.

Test 2 - Granger causality (Granger 1969): Tests whether lagged noise predicts greenium beyond what lagged greenium alone predicts, and vice versa. One-directional Granger causality from noise to greenium supports H2.

8.1 - Lead-lag event study around high-noise episodes¶

In [19]:
print("H2 LEAD-LAG EVENT STUDY - High-Noise Episodes (above P75)")
print("=" * 65)

for country in ["India", "Indonesia"]:
    country_panel = panel[panel["country"]==country].copy().sort_values("date").reset_index(drop=True)
    threshold = country_panel["signaling_noise"].quantile(0.75)
    print(f"\n[{country}]  High-noise threshold (P75): {threshold:.4f}")
    
    high_noise_dates = country_panel[country_panel["signaling_noise"] > threshold]["date"].unique()
    print(f"  High-noise episodes: {len(high_noise_dates)}")
    
    records = []
    for event_date in high_noise_dates:
        window = country_panel[
            (country_panel["date"] >= event_date - pd.Timedelta(days=7)) &
            (country_panel["date"] <= event_date + pd.Timedelta(days=7))
        ].copy()
        window["event_time_h2"] = (window["date"] - event_date).dt.days
        records.append(window)
    
    if not records:
        print("  No episodes found."); continue
    
    es_h2 = pd.concat(records, ignore_index=True).dropna(subset=["greenium_fd"]).copy()
    es_h2["event_time_h2"] = es_h2["event_time_h2"].astype(int)
    print(f"  Event-window obs: {len(es_h2):,}")
    
    ev_dummies = pd.get_dummies(es_h2["event_time_h2"].astype(str), drop_first=False, dtype=float)
    if "-1" in ev_dummies.columns: ev_dummies = ev_dummies.drop(columns=["-1"])
    es_h2_reg = pd.concat([es_h2, ev_dummies], axis=1)
    ev_cols_h2 = list(ev_dummies.columns)
    
    if len(ev_cols_h2) < 2: print("  Insufficient variation."); continue
    
    X = sm.add_constant(es_h2_reg[ev_cols_h2])
    model_h2 = OLS(es_h2_reg["greenium_fd"], X).fit(cov_type="HC3")
    
    print(f"  Lead-lag coefficients (ref: day -1)")
    print(f"  {'Day':<6} {'Coef':>10} {'p':>8} {'Sig':<5} {'Interpretation'}")
    print(f"  {'-'*60}")
    for day in range(-5, 6):
        if day == -1:
            print(f"  {day:<6} {'0.000':>10} {'---':>8} {'ref':<5} reference"); continue
        col = str(day)
        if col in model_h2.params.index:
            c = model_h2.params[col]; p = model_h2.pvalues[col]
            s = "***" if p<0.01 else "**" if p<0.05 else "*" if p<0.1 else ""
            interp = "PRE-SPIKE should be flat" if day < 0 else "POST-SPIKE H2 response"
            print(f"  {day:<6} {c:>+10.4f} {p:>8.3f} {s:<5} {interp}")
    
    pre_sig = sum(1 for d in range(-5,-1)
                  if str(d) in model_h2.params.index and model_h2.pvalues[str(d)] < 0.1)
    verdict = "Pre-spike flat: consistent with noise->greenium" if pre_sig==0 else "Pre-spike movement: possible reverse causality"
    print(f"  Pre-spike significant days (expect 0): {pre_sig}  ->  {verdict}")

8.2 - Granger causality test¶

In [20]:
print("GRANGER CAUSALITY - Does Signaling Noise Granger-cause the Greenium?")
print("=" * 65)
print("H0: X does NOT Granger-cause Y")
print("Rejection -> X has predictive power over future Y beyond Y own lags")
print()

for country in ["India", "Indonesia"]:
    sub = panel_fd[panel_fd["country"]==country][
        ["date","greenium_fd","signaling_noise_fd"]
    ].dropna().copy()
    
    print(f"[{country}]  N={len(sub):,}")
    print(f"  Direction 1: Noise -> Greenium")
    res_fwd = grangercausalitytests(sub[["greenium_fd","signaling_noise_fd"]].values, maxlag=5, verbose=False)
    for lag, r in res_fwd.items():
        f=r[0]["ssr_ftest"][0]; p=r[0]["ssr_ftest"][1]
        s="***" if p<0.01 else "**" if p<0.05 else "*" if p<0.1 else "n.s."
        print(f"    Lag {lag}: F={f:.3f}  p={p:.3f}  {s}")
    
    print(f"  Direction 2: Greenium -> Noise (reverse)")
    res_rev = grangercausalitytests(sub[["signaling_noise_fd","greenium_fd"]].values, maxlag=5, verbose=False)
    for lag, r in res_rev.items():
        f=r[0]["ssr_ftest"][0]; p=r[0]["ssr_ftest"][1]
        s="***" if p<0.01 else "**" if p<0.05 else "*" if p<0.1 else "n.s."
        print(f"    Lag {lag}: F={f:.3f}  p={p:.3f}  {s}")
    print()

print("INTERPRETATION:")
print("  Noise->Greenium sig, reverse not -> H2 directional support")
print("  Both significant -> bidirectional, H2 needs careful qualification")
print("  Neither significant -> no Granger-causal ordering")

Part 9 - Summary of All Findings¶

In [21]:
print("=" * 65)
print("EVENT STUDY COMPLETE SUMMARY")
print("=" * 65)

for label, weeks, coefs_, pvals_ in [
    ("POOLED",    all_weeks,     coefs,     pvals),
    ("INDIA",     all_weeks_ind, coefs_ind, p_ind),
    ("INDONESIA", all_weeks_ido, coefs_ido, p_ido),
]:
    pre_coefs  = [c for w,c in zip(weeks,coefs_) if w < -1]
    post_coefs = [c for w,c in zip(weeks,coefs_) if w > 0]
    pre_sig    = sum(1 for w,p in zip(weeks,pvals_) if w < -1 and p < 0.1)
    post_sig   = sum(1 for w,p in zip(weeks,pvals_) if w > 0  and p < 0.1)
    
    print(f"\n[{label}]")
    print(f"  Pre-event:   mean beta = {np.mean(pre_coefs):+.5f} pp | sig weeks = {pre_sig}/{len(pre_coefs)}")
    print(f"  Post-event:  mean beta = {np.mean(post_coefs):+.5f} pp | sig weeks = {post_sig}/{len(post_coefs)}")
    pt = "SUPPORTED" if pre_sig == 0 else f"VIOLATED ({pre_sig} pre-event weeks significant)"
    te = "DETECTED"  if post_sig > 0 else "NOT DETECTED (null result)"
    print(f"  Parallel trends (H3): {pt}")
    print(f"  Treatment effect (H3): {te}")

print()

Appendix - Econometric notes¶

Reference category¶

Week -1 (immediately before treatment) is the standard omitted category in event studies. All beta_k coefficients measure deviation from the immediate pre-treatment level. This is consistent with MacKinlay (1997) and Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021).

Weekly binning¶

Trading-day distances are binned into 5-day (approximately 1 calendar week) intervals using floor(event_time / 5). This reduces the number of dummies and improves statistical power. Within-week dynamics are averaged out.

Pair FE in pooled vs country-specific regressions¶

Pair FE are essential in the pooled regression to absorb the level difference between India (mean greenium ~ +0.005 pp) and Indonesia (mean greenium ~ -0.069 pp). Without them, the constant conflates two structurally different markets. In country-specific regressions, one pair means pair FE are collinear with the constant and are omitted.

Key references¶

  • MacKinlay, A.C. (1997). Event studies in economics and finance. Journal of Economic Literature, 35(1), 13-39.
  • Callaway, B. and Sant'Anna, P. (2021). DiD with multiple time periods. Journal of Econometrics, 225(2), 200-230.
  • Roth, J. (2022). Pre-test with caution. American Economic Review: Insights, 4(3), 305-322.
  • Granger, C.W.J. (1969). Investigating causal relations. Econometrica, 37(3), 424-438.
  • Sun, L. and Abraham, S. (2021). Estimating dynamic treatment effects. Journal of Econometrics, 225(2), 175-199.
